status_definitions.faithful_translation: Checked translation or complete reconstruction of the cited definitions/statements; its explicit hypotheses are retained.
status_definitions.derived_simplification: Human proof or additional elementary consequence derived from the cited setup; not claimed to be literally the same source statement.
status_definitions.remaining_input: A precisely located hypothesis/result whose actual arithmetic proof or final-family witness remains unreconstructed.

claims.title: Decorated hermitian lattices and explicit polynomial coefficients
claims.statement: The models use decorated unimodular lattices in the standard hermitian space over a CM field. The coefficient modules are tensor products of polynomial dual-Weyl modules, with Weyl and dual-Weyl integral companions transported by local basis matrices; columns use the contragredient module evaluated on Lsharp, rows the direct module evaluated on N.
assumptions: The Fields.Ok and lattice/decorations hypotheses of the source are in force.
claims.source_relation: Definitions translated; the quantitative integrality and duality results are separately retained as PL16.

claims.title: Equivariant functions and pointwise integral lattices
claims.statement: After finite orbit and stabilizer theorems, equivariant functions identify with a finite direct sum of stabilizer-invariant coefficient spaces. Integral forms take values in the chosen Del or Nab coefficient lattice at every decorated point.
assumptions: Finite orbit set; finite stabilizers; equivariance of coefficient lattices.

claims.title: Finite kernel formula and actual bilinear period
claims.statement: A covariant kernel acts by the stabilizer-weighted finite orbit sum. Chains compose such maps, with a final coupled finite sum where applicable. The final period is the stabilizer-weighted sum of the normalized bilinear Fock pairing of br_u applied to the terminal column value with the row value. colPer_eq identifies this concrete period with the chain-factorized abstract period.
assumptions: Finite classes and stabilizers at every stage; supplied theta kernels and their covariance; the stated terminal branching map.
claims.source_relation: The individual arithmetic theta-kernel formulas and their estimates are not reconstructed by this finite-sum translation; see PL15.

claims.title: Ramified source space, lattice, and retained rank
claims.statement: The initial source is the joint kernel of residue-unit averaging at P dividing the chosen CM element piT(u), with the pointwise Del lattice intersected into that subspace. ramDim and ramBas are the dimension and a basis of this ramified K-space. The full dimension duS and retained ramified dimension du differ by the explicit RamRank factor.
assumptions: Fullness of the coefficient function lattice; FreeRankModel and HidaSetting for the displayed rank formula.
claims.source_relation: The averaging index set is divs(piT), not all primes over rational T. No equality du=duS is claimed.

claims.title: Selected row space and projected row lattice
claims.statement: The good row subspace is selected by the product of the finite-group character projector and level-character projector. Mt is the pointwise Nab lattice intersected with this subspace. Pq is the hermitian orthogonal projection to the selected rational theta-adjoint part in coordinates. The quotient lattice is Pq(Mt); the intersection lattice cutZ is a distinct object.
assumptions: Metric positivity and the source rationality/stability assumptions for the selected subspaces.
claims.source_relation: The 1/|P| row metric normalization is retained. Auxiliary finite-group characters are not the outer Dirichlet target character.

claims.title: Rational common theta quotient is an arithmetic input
claims.statement: For the actual models, all complex maps J_t on the selected row quotients must be injective with the same selected image, and J_0^{-1}J_t must have coefficients in K. Given these facts the code defines iota_t by rowMat, with base value identity.
assumptions: H2 and RATmu; the chosen rational quotient coordinates and nondegenerate metrics.
claims.source_relation: The definitions of rowMat and kMat alone do not establish rationality. The theta rationality/common-image theorems are not proved in this reconstruction.

claims.title: Canonical quotient descent of B_u
claims.statement: If the base period kills ker(pi_0), then B_u(phi,y)=P_{u,0}(phi,r y), for any K-linear right inverse r, is the unique bilinear descent. It is independent of r.
assumptions: pi_0 is K-linear and surjective; P_{u,0} vanishes on its kernel.
claims.source_relation: The source makes the same right-inverse definition and proves factorization; independence and uniqueness are supplied here as a short basis-free consequence.

claims.title: Rationalizing the complex scalar, including zero periods
claims.statement: Given xi sigma(P)=sigma(B composed with iota pi), choose eta=xi^{-1} over K when xi lies in sigma(K). If xi does not lie in sigma(K), every period value vanishes, since a nonzero one expresses xi as a quotient of two K-values; then eta=1 works. The MIUnit2 finite-place assumption makes eta a unit at the selected place, without requiring B nonzero.
assumptions: The complex comparison identity; xi is nonzero and its base value is 1; any K-preimage of xi at the selected parameter is a finite-place unit.
claims.source_relation: The scalar in PairingFactorsThroughPeriods is the inverse of the scalar in MatrixIdentityOffBase; the main fragment tracks this inversion.

claims.title: Explicit common row lattice, fullness and uniqueness
claims.statement: R is the intersection over finite places of the localizations of iota_{mu(w)} pi_{mu(w)} Mt. Because mu is the base parameter outside finitely many places, all local modules can be glued into a full O_K-lattice; its localizations are exactly prescribed, and it is unique. A complete proof by primary decomposition of a finite torsion module is supplied.
assumptions: Full Mt; surjective pi_t; bijective iota_t; finite exceptional set for mu.
claims.source_relation: Our proof uses standard primary decomposition of finite torsion O_K-modules. Localizations are inside the rational vector space, not completions.

claims.title: Shifted integral maps into the one common dual lattice
claims.statement: If local periods have ord_w at least sigma_u(w) unless zero, and their rational comparison scalar is a w-unit, then B_u(I_u N_u,R) is integral for I_u=product p_w^{-floor sigma_u(w)}. More generally the result holds for any finitely supported integer k_u(w)<=ceil sigma_u(w). The same R is independent of u.
assumptions: Full source lattice; finite support of shifts; local period valuation bound; eta a local unit; exact row localizations.
claims.source_relation: The zero alternative is kept explicitly. Allowing k<=ceil is already in the source; no claim is made that replacing every actual floor by ceil preserves all family records.

claims.title: Exact norm descent and the chain-height inequality
claims.statement: Descent through a quotient with its quotient metric preserves functional norm. With final pairing bound p_v, chain operator bounds a_{j,v}, and lower squared norm factor s_v for the identification into the common metric space, ||B||_v^2<=p_v^2 product a_{j,v}^2/s_v. The source uses s_v=kappa_v min_p product_j lambda_{j,p,v}; taking the mean of logarithms preserves the order mean_v min_p. Logarithmic height is used only for B nonzero.
assumptions: Positive definite metrics and quotient metric; the base chain factorization; positive norm majorants; p ranges over a finite nonempty spectral index set; kappa_v>0 and every lambda_{j,p,v}>0; spectral lower norm bound at every infinite place; B nonzero when ordinary logarithmic height is taken.
claims.source_relation: The proof in the fragment is a compact human reconstruction. Quantitative kernel/eigenvalue estimates remain PL15. The source uses squared norms and equal means over infinite places in the totally complex setting.

claims.title: Coordinate source pullback and exact fractional-ideal shift
claims.statement: The bridge coordinate lattice is Cons.nuOf=eNu^{-1}(L.NuLat). NprimeDef specifies the final lattice as I_u L.NuLat, with I_u=product p_w^{-floor(e_w sg_u(w))}. shift_nuOf proves this becomes shiftLat in coordinates; sigma_u(w)=e_w sg_u(w). Negative exponents and negative gains are permitted.
assumptions: The record condition NprimeDef and the coordinate lattice tie.
claims.source_relation: The floor is after multiplication by the ramification index. The coordinate pullback introduces no new choice of source lattice.

claims.title: Final restricted source witness and its local conditions remain to be tied
claims.statement: The final bridge supplies the source lattice through L.NuLat and record ties. NuDef gives local inclusion in Mram away from the own type prime T_u, equality at specified dropped/non-inert places, and normalization of local length. Its actual witness and transport from local gate lattices have not been reconstructed here. Local index bounds use full duS while slopes divide by the retained ramified rank.
assumptions: The final family witness and all compatibility maps must be supplied.
claims.source_relation: NuDef excludes T_u from the regular inclusion condition. The repository constructor recorded in PL14 has not been tied to the headline route and is not substituted for this witness.

claims.title: A concrete available source-lattice constructor; headline-route use unconfirmed
claims.statement: NZColD.nuLat intersects explicit local conditions: a scaled ramified U-operator lattice at T_u; inverse image of a gate lattice NPf at selected gate primes; and the localized initial ramified lattice elsewhere. This is an available source definition. A search did not establish that sizeDataNu is the witness used in the headline RH route.
assumptions: Finite selected gate-prime support, local absorption/fullness assumptions in NuData, and transport identifications.
claims.source_relation: Excluded from the main fragment as a claimed final witness. Status applies only to the translated definition, not to its use on the headline call path.

claims.title: Actual theta comparison, kernel estimates and spectral bounds remain inputs
claims.statement: MIid compares algebraic periods with complex theta/Hilbert pairings using norm-preserving U_u,V, a conjugate-linear row map sEE, a nonzero scalar a_u, and comparison scalars xi_{u,t}. MIstar2 requires the unit-compatible comparison and a_u nonzero. Along with rational common-image and coordinate/metric conditions this yields rational factorization and L1e. The present proof does not derive MIid, the individual theta kernels, their valuation estimates, or their all-place norm/spectral bounds.
assumptions: All source theta and arithmetic comparison hypotheses; spectral lower bounds and operator upper bounds at every infinite place.
claims.source_relation: The scalar a_u is nonzero, not asserted to be unit modulus. The conjugate-linearity of sEE makes the complex Hilbert expression bilinear. MIUnit2 is weaker than a root-of-unity hypothesis.

claims.title: Coefficient lattice and finite-class arithmetic facts not expanded quantitatively
claims.statement: The source proves the transported Nab/Del modules are full lattices, Del is contained in Nab, and the actual decorated-point models have finite classes and stabilizers. These declarations support the finite model used here; their arithmetic denominator, duality and quantitative estimates are not reconstructed in this pass.
assumptions: Full underlying O_E-lattice; Fields.Ok; algebraic representation and local transport conditions.
claims.source_relation: No new proof of the deep coefficient or class-number estimates is claimed. The elementary finite-function consequence is PL17.

claims.title: Elementary finite-model consequences
claims.statement: A finite direct sum of invariant subspaces has a full pointwise function lattice whenever the equivariant coefficient lattices are full: clear denominators of an invariant-space K-basis and use Noetherian finite generation. Covariance also makes the weighted kernel independent of orbit representatives, because stabilizers are conjugate and rho factors cancel.
assumptions: Finite orbit set; finite stabilizers; full equivariant coefficient lattices; kernel covariance.
claims.source_relation: Complete short proofs are in report section 2. They use no averaging denominators for lattice fullness.

claims.title: Orthogonality gives the theta kernel vanishing needed for descent
claims.statement: If Theta(W) lies in E0 and Theta*(E0) lies in W, then F in W orthogonal to Theta*(E0) satisfies ||Theta F||^2=<F,Theta*Theta F>=0. Applied to the kernel of the selected quotient, this gives the base period kernel vanishing once the theta identity and rational coordinate compatibility are supplied.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional positive definite Hilbert spaces; the displayed image/adjoint inclusions; quotient kernel orthogonality; the actual theta-period identity for the application.
claims.source_relation: Basis-free human compression of the source coordinate proof; no assertion that the required rationality/level compatibility hypotheses hold without further input.

claims.title: DIVRecBridgeSel is a package and compatibility bridge
claims.statement: DivisionKernelData ties the actual column record to the selected row family. DivisionKernelConstantBounds provides, uniformly for sufficiently late family members, the required packages and rationality/fullness fields. linkDIVt_of_bridge_kernel transports these hypotheses to LinkDIVt; it is not itself a formula or proof for the arithmetic theta kernels.
assumptions: All fields of the package, with their stated late-family quantifiers; numerical and model compatibility ties.
claims.source_relation: This records the exact entry point requested by the parent. No closed proof of the input fields has been reconstructed here.

claims.title: Four distinct outputs of the divisibility/height package
claims.statement: DivClauses exports common shifted-source integrality, positive pointwise squared-norm majorants with prescribed mean logarithm, a numerical row/divisibility inequality, and the exact shifted source-slope identity. The positive-majorant formulation also handles a zero B_u without taking an ordinary logarithm of zero.
assumptions: All DivInputs and row/column well-formedness hypotheses, including local divisibility and all-place norm bounds.
claims.source_relation: The main fragment proves the algebraic/analytic operations producing the first, norm part of the second, and their bridge. Quantitative arithmetic inequalities and exact parameter values are not asserted to have been reconstructed.
